annotations.source:
# The worked example for the native-annotation syntax: the Boys function and
# the primitive Gaussian overlap from the SCF programs, annotated at all three
# levels, with two labeled regions and a variable glossary.
#
# The annotations are ordinary comments to the compiler, so this file compiles
# and runs exactly as the stripped version would. `viv doc annotated.viv`
# extracts them; `viv src annotated.viv boys_F0` prints the stripped source.
#
# Validation: a normalized Gaussian overlapping itself is exactly 1.

pi = 3.141592653589793

#[ The one special function: everything with a 1/r in it funnels through F0
#| Series branch: the closed form has a 0/0 at T = 0, so small arguments switch to Taylor
#|| Three terms reach 1e-8 accuracy below the branch cutoff
#: T  the squared distance times the reduced exponent; the only argument F0 has
def boys_F0(T) {
    if T < 1.0e-8 {
        return 1.0 - T / 3.0 + T * T / 10.0
    }
    #| The definition, integrated as written: F0(T) = integral of exp(-T t^2) over [0,1]
    #|| Simpson quadrature, 60 panels -- slow per call, transparently correct
    #||| Production codes use tables and rational fits; this program optimizes for legibility
    return simpson(fn(t) -> exp(-T * t * t), 0.0, 1.0, 60)
}
#]

#[ Overlap of two normalized s-Gaussians
#| The Gaussian product theorem does all the work: two centers collapse to one
#~ integrals, gaussian
#: a   exponent of the bra primitive
#: b   exponent of the ket primitive
#: r2  squared distance between the two centers
#: p   the combined exponent a + b, the center of the product Gaussian
def prim_overlap(a, b, r2) {
    p = a + b
    #| K carries the distance penalty between the two centers
    #: K  the Gaussian-product prefactor exp(-ab/p * r2)
    K = exp(-a * b / p * r2)
    #|| The (2a/pi)^(3/4) factors normalize each primitive on the fly
    #||| Baking these into contraction coefficients is the usual optimization; explicit keeps every formula matching the textbook
    #: Na  normalization of the bra s-primitive
    #: Nb  normalization of the ket s-primitive
    Na = pow(2.0 * a / pi, 0.75)
    Nb = pow(2.0 * b / pi, 0.75)
    return Na * Nb * pow(pi / p, 1.5) * K
}
#]

#| A normalized Gaussian overlapping itself must give exactly 1
show prim_overlap(0.9, 0.9, 0.0)

test "self-overlap of a normalized primitive is 1" {
    assert_near(prim_overlap(0.9, 0.9, 0.0), 1.0, 1.0e-12)
}
